relevance.rationale: This is the toolkit the keystone conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-symbol is currently being worked with, supplied at theorem strength and with the 4_1 case computed explicitly. The block's own authorNotes name exactly this machinery -- 'formal q-Borel diagonal-invariant mismatch', 'numeric connection-matrix theta-growth q^{m^2/4}', Newton-polygon slopes and RSZ isoclinicity -- while the corpus has no reference for any of it. The paper defines a class of linear q-difference equations (modular q-holonomic modules) whose fundamental matrices at 0 and infinity have *computable* monodromy, gives an algorithm for the fundamental matrix (Sec 2.2) and the q-Borel/q-Laplace resummation used to build it (Sec 2.3), proves the generalised q-hypergeometric equation is modular and self-dual (Thm 1.4), and devotes Sec 5 to the q-difference equation of the 4_1 knot -- monodromy, residues, determinants, state integral, and an analytic lift of the coloured Jones polynomial. The 4_1 equation and the Faddeev quantum dilogarithm state-integral factorisation are the same objects prop:habiro-tail-archimedean-action and the QBeta 4_1 probes evaluate. Caveat kept explicit: no theorem here is a drop-in lemma for a named QOU sorry -- the paper supplies the framework and the 4_1 computation, not the prolongation-symbol identification, so no aid-proof is claimed.

The probe's empirical growth exponent can be checked against these theta entries instead of being left as a numeric observation.

relevance.rationale: Introduces MODULAR q-holonomic modules -- those whose fundamental matrices define an SL(2,Z) cocycle with improved analyticity, extending from the cut plane across the unit circle -- proves the generalised q-hypergeometric equation is modular and self-dual, and shows that three key q-holonomic modules of complex Chern--Simons theory are modular; an alternative title the authors give is 'Modular linear q-difference equations', and the stated payoff is an EFFECTIVE METHOD to solve the corresponding linear q-difference equations, with fundamental solutions whose residues are expressed in terms of the solutions themselves. This lands squarely on the corpus's active front. The bibliography already carries the peacock-patterns paper (registered as the structural fact that Stokes constants are integer Donaldson--Thomas invariants of the associated q-difference structure) and the Borel-summability paper for 4_1 and 5_2, and an audit records a Stokes-matrix identification target for the 4_1 descendant equation; the corpus is chasing solutions and Stokes data of exactly the q-difference equations this document makes effectively solvable, and has no entry for it. The corpus's own Im(q) framing also matters here: this document's improved analyticity is precisely about crossing |q| = 1, the boundary between the corpus's fibre-level formal q and its archimedean real q_0, so the modularity property is relevant to how the two levels connect rather than merely a technical convenience.

keyResults.locator: Def. 1.1 with Thm 1.2 (the slash operator), and Thm 1.4
keyResults.statement: A q-difference equation is modular when the monodromy relation holds for all of SL(2,Z); it suffices to check the generators S and T, and the generalised q-hypergeometric equation is modular and self-dual with the two natural cocycles equal.
keyResults.useForFolio: A checkable criterion (two generators) for the modularity of the q-difference equations the corpus works with, and with it the effective solution method the Stokes-matrix work currently lacks.

keyResults.locator: Sec. 1.5 (modular q-holonomic modules in Chern--Simons theory), Thm 1.5
keyResults.statement: Three q-holonomic modules arising in complex Chern--Simons theory are modular, with explicitly computed monodromy and cocycles.
keyResults.useForFolio: Places the corpus's own state-integral and descendant equations inside a class with computable monodromy, which is the missing ingredient in the Stokes-matrix identification target for the figure-eight descendant equation.

proposedActions.rationale: The corpus registers two companion papers on resurgence and Stokes data in complex Chern--Simons but not the one that supplies the effective solution method for the underlying q-difference equations.

The improved analyticity across |q| = 1 is directly about the boundary between the corpus's fibre-level formal q and its archimedean real q_0, a distinction AGENTS.md flags as a recurring source of confusion; a remark connecting modularity to that boundary would be more useful than a bare citation.
